opening.argument: The presentation promotes an official-sounding $300 LUNA airdrop as “100% real” and urges viewers to join quickly. The speaker tells viewers, “then you will get tera token of around $ 300,” while directing them through a claim process. That process leads to an external form requesting the email associated with a CoinMarketCap account, an existing 8-digit Binance user ID, and a LUNA wallet address and memo, followed by submission. These are not merely general promotional claims: viewers are actively encouraged to participate and provide account and wallet information in order to receive tokens. The combination of a promised low-barrier reward, urgency, and collection of identifying account and wallet details establishes the deceptive acquisition scheme presented here.
